working_title: The FBI Raided the Wrong House. The Government Said Checking the Address Was Optional.
one_line: A six-man FBI SWAT team blew open the front door of 3756 Denville Trace at dawn, flash-banged a family that had done nothing, and then argued in court for eight years that failing to read the house number on the mailbox was a protected policy judgement.
contradiction: They were the wrong house, the government admitted it, and for eight years its legal answer was that nobody could be held responsible because deciding whether to check the address was a discretionary policy choice.
scored_by: claude, 2026-08-12, v002 rubric, for the 45-minute slot

justification.personal_relevance: The point of contact is the viewer's own front door at 4 a.m. There is no denser contact point in the rubric's list; a house is the one system every single viewer touches every night. 15.
justification.wtf_factor: Two of them, both on the record. The agent threw his GPS away after the raid, and the United States argued that checking the street sign and the house number 'involved the kind of policy judgments that the discretionary-function exception was designed to protect'. 15.
justification.human_stakes: The honest limiter. Injuries, property damage, a terrified 7-year-old, no compensation for eight years -- but nobody died, nobody went to prison, no house or life savings was lost. 11 of 15, not 15, and the film must not pretend otherwise.
justification.contradiction: Innocent family, wrong address, and the very FTCA amendment Congress passed in 1974 BECAUSE of wrong-house raids was read by the Eleventh Circuit to leave them with nothing. Maximum.
justification.story_arc: Ordinary night, then the raid, then it gets worse (summary judgment for the government, affirmed on appeal), then a unanimous Supreme Court reversal, then remand -- and still no trial in 2026. Full arc plus a live tail. 10.
justification.title_power: Subject-verb-consequence lands cleanly and the verb is 'raided'. Loses one point because the second clause needs the word 'address' to carry, which is one beat more than the cleanest PD titles. 9.
justification.thumbnail_power: One image: a splintered residential front door with a house number on it. Single subject, no explanation needed. 9, not 10, only because no photograph of that specific door has been located yet.
justification.evidence: A Supreme Court slip opinion, a published district-court opinion at 631 F. Supp. 3d 1281 with the deposition detail, the cert-stage appendix, and public-domain oral-argument audio from 29 April 2025. Everything can go on screen. 10.
justification.broad_audience: It requires no interest in law, policing or policy. A door, a family, a mistake. 10.
justification.franchiseability: Wrong-house raids are a documented genre: Collinsville 1973 (Giglotto and Askew, cited in the concurrence), Onree Norris, Amir Locke, Karen Jimerson. Ten to a hundred is plausible. 5.
justification.evergreen: The holding is now the governing federal rule and the case is unresolved. Watchable in five years. 5.
justification.real_footage: United States Supreme Court oral-argument audio, No. 24-362, argued 29 April 2025 -- a US Government work, public domain, indexed in the shelf's own Oyez case index as 'martin v united states -> [[2024, 24-362]]'. Genuine recorded voices of this case arguing itself.
justification.recognizable_institution: The FBI and the Supreme Court of the United States, both central rather than incidental.
justification.major_reversal: Summary judgment for the government, affirmed by the Eleventh Circuit, then vacated by a unanimous Supreme Court on 12 June 2025.
